sources_considered.why: Primary mismatch-detection evaluation; relevant but not a direct test of the complete self-checking and corrective-feedback task.
Primary human validation of automated checks on generated images; material evidence of useful checking ability.
Automated ranking is relevant background, but does not directly establish accurate detection of prompt and feedback violations.
Evaluates a later image-generation system outside the historical scope.

evidence_items.locator: Section 1; related experimental findings in sections 4.2 and 5
evidence_items.explanation: FineMatch finds weaknesses in compositional mismatch analysis by GPT-4V and Gemini Pro Vision, while reporting improvements from task-specific training. Its benchmark does not directly measure a generator checking its own outputs against successive user corrections.

evidence_items.locator: Introduction, contribution 2; section 3 and appendix A.3
evidence_items.explanation: ConceptMix reports 0.81 consistency between GPT-4o and human-majority judgments, compared with 0.85 among human evaluators. This challenges a blanket characterization of checking as poor, but uses decomposed concept questions rather than the full self-checking and feedback task.

unresolved_gaps: No located evaluation directly covers both checking a system's own generated images and checking compliance with corrective feedback.
The available studies use different tasks and measures, so they do not establish a common failure rate for the claimed capability.
The evidence does not establish whether substantially new technology was necessary.
